result.title: Counterfactual Test-Time Augmentation for Shortcut Removal in Language Models
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) can exploit shortcuts, i.e., correlations present in training data that may not hold at test time. This can lead to poor predictions when correlations shift. Most existing solutions for removing shortcuts operate at training time, requiring labeled training data, model weight access, and significant computational resources. Here, we study the problem of test-time shortcut removal. We propose a family of counterfactual test-time augmentation (CTTA) methods: given an example, each method uses an auxiliary model to generate counterfactual edits in which the shortcut value is changed, and then takes a weighted average of the LLM's predictions across these edits. We prove that the optimal shortcut-invariant predictor is a member of this CTTA family, and we characterize its weights. The weights depend on the training distribution, and therefore are, in general, not identifiable from the trained model and unlabeled test data. However, we present assumptions under which the weights can be obtained using the token probabilities of the trained LLM, and propose tests to detect violations of these assumptions. We use these tests to develop Select-CTTA, an aggregate method that selects among CTTA methods. Empirically, we find that Select-CTTA outperforms test-time baselines and approaches the performance of models fine-tuned on shortcut-balanced data.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究语言模型在测试时去除捷径（shortcut）的问题，提出 CTTA 方法族：用辅助模型对输入做改变捷径取值的反事实编辑，再对 LLM 在各编辑下的预测加权平均；证明最优捷径不变预测器属于该族并刻画其权重，给出权重可由 token 概率得到的假设与违例检验，并据此提出 Select-CTTA。
